# CAPR Copilot instructions

## Build, test, and lint commands
- Start the default dev stack from the repo root with `docker compose up -d`, then run `caddy run --config Caddyfile.dev` and use `http://localhost:5002`.
- Frontend commands live in `frontend/`: `npm run dev`, `npm run build`, and `npm run check`.
- Germanic validation: `docs/CI_VALIDATION.md` distinguishes portable checks from strict holding/runtime checks. Use targeted pytest selectors under `Germanic/tests/`; a portable pass does not certify original PDFs or fresh Foma execution.
- Default book: `bash Germanic/docs/assembly/build_capr_book_draft_docker.sh`. See `Germanic/docs/assembly/README.md` for standalone presentations and publication checks.

## High-level architecture
- CAPR is a shared Flask API in `backend/` plus a Svelte UI in `frontend/`, used by three parallel research pipelines: Germanic, Burmish, and Celtic.
- `docker-compose.yml` mounts Germanic data, FSTs, tools, and docs into `/usr/app` by default, so the running backend operates on Germanic unless those volume mounts are changed.
- `/new-board` calls `compile_to_json_full_cognates()` to ingest TSV rows into the shared board payload (`boards`, `columns`, `words`, `syllables`, `fstDoculects`, `dataProfile`); `data_profiles.py` auto-detects the dataset family and decides how `syllables_parsed` is built.
- `/compare-fst` and `/refish-board` compile Foma text in temporary directories, load doculect bins through the mappings in `compare_fst.py` and `refish.py`, and return correspondence output or reassigned boards; missing bins are surfaced as `missing_transducers`.
- `frontend/src/App.svelte` owns board and FST state, persists boards and FST text to `localStorage`, and derives the default transducer from the selected TSV prefix; `frontend/src/api.ts` honors `window.__CAPR_API_BASE__` when present, otherwise tries `/api` before direct backend ports.
- `frontend/src/FstComparator.svelte` and `frontend/src/FstOutput.svelte` expect `compare_fst.py` to return `chapters`, `errors`, and `missing_transducers`; the backend groups correspondences by syllable position (`i/m/r/t`), and the UI pads blank reconstruction cells back in for skipped languages instead of collapsing columns while rendering the result through a virtual list.

## Key conventions
- Any command that uses `foma` or `flookup`, or Python scripts that shell out to them, should run inside the backend container rather than against a host-local install.
- Before debugging FST behavior, confirm the environment first: make sure `docker compose ps` is healthy, then verify `/usr/app`, `/usr/app/fsts`, and `foma`/`flookup` inside the backend container before changing code. For Germanic adjudication, `python3 Germanic/tools/adjudicate.py SCNNN --evidence` performs the container rebuild and firing census for you.
- When compiling `Germanic/fsts/germanic.txt`, always include `-e quit`; the file does not terminate on its own and otherwise leaves `foma` hanging.
- New TSVs are not automatically exposed in the UI: `backend/server.py` allowlists the visible datasets in `list_inputs()`, and `frontend/src/App.svelte` derives the default transducer name from the dataset prefix (`germanic-aligned-final.tsv` -> `germanic.txt`), so each visible dataset also needs a matching `<prefix>.txt` under `fsts/`.
- Exported lowercase transducer names must still line up with the doculect-to-bin mappings in `compare_fst.py` and `refish.py`.
- Preserve `dataProfile` and `syllables_parsed` when changing board payloads; `compare_fst.py` uses those parsed slots to build Initial/Medial/Rime/Tone correspondence chapters and only backfills from the TSV as a fallback.
- Refishing depends on the "Use new FST?" toggle: when it is on, `/refish-board` compiles the editor text; when it is off, `refish.py` falls back to `backend/refishing-fst2.txt`, loads whatever mapped `*.bin` files exist, and skips unknown or missing doculect bins with log lines instead of failing the whole request.
- If you are reproducing a blank-FST UI issue, follow `docs/USAGE.md`: switch to the FST editor before loading the dataset and use `Debug`; loading from the board view with an empty transducer can freeze the page.
- When touching Foma rules, keep network names short, avoid optional-context parentheses in replacement rules, and make sure disabled definitions are not still composed elsewhere; all three are common failure modes here (details preserved in `docs/archive/legacy-agent-workflow.md`).
- For Germanic work, start with `Germanic/docs/README.md` for task routing and ownership, and `CURRENT_STATE.md` for the live programme. Archived records and old packets never override current SOURCE.
- Use `adjudicate.py` for scientific preparation/evidence/finalization and `python3 Germanic/tools/adjudicate.py --refresh` after SOURCE edits. `artifact_graph.py` is the sole generated-output owner; never hand-edit projections or invoke a hand-picked generator list. `registry/CONTROL_PLANE.md` defines SOURCE and frozen authority.
- Lexical research/source verification starts at `Germanic/docs/lexeme_reports/pgmc_reconstructions/README.md`; editorial selection at `report_schema.md` and `pgmc_integration/README.md`. Preserve mature `.model.md` prose and source ledgers. Archived per-entry checklists and implementation reports are not new drafting obligations.
- Any agent touching Germanic sound-change history, chronology, historical staging or scope, FST rule semantics, or interaction/chronology evidence MUST read and follow `Germanic/docs/RESEARCH_ADJUDICATION_PROTOCOL.md` and record its work using `Germanic/docs/sound_changes/audits/ADJUDICATION_TEMPLATE.md`. In particular: never infer historical stage or domain from an FST identifier prefix or executable environment, and never promote a chronology edge merely because a lexeme changes in the interaction harness.
- Instruction precedence for Germanic adjudication tasks: the explicit user instruction, then the research protocol, then this file. `docs/AGENTS.md` is only a short routing rule pointing at the adjudication interface; an explicit user request to complete, commit and push an adjudication is itself the authorization for those operations (the archived legacy workflow in `docs/archive/legacy-agent-workflow.md` is never an instruction source).
- Reader-facing Germanic sound-change chapters are rule-centered: one `define` per `foma` block, labelled rule sections, SC-number-plus-rule-name cross-references, page-numbered citations, italicized Old English forms with first-mention single-quoted glosses, raw LaTeX `\emph{*form}` for reconstructed forms, and no file paths or internal IDs in chapter prose.
